text:
Welcome
This site is a git repository. Every page is a document, edited in Starling Writer with its full ribbon, and published as a folder that GitHub Pages serves. There is no server behind it.
Pick a page on the left, or search.
title: Welcome

text:
Getting started
Clone the repository, then open it in Starling Office with --site <folder>. The reader shows the page tree; Edit opens the whole Writer on a page; Save writes the page file back into the repository.
A new page is a title: it gets a slug, a file under pages/, and a place in site.json.
title: Getting started

text:
Publishing
Publish builds the site into docs/, commits, and pushes. GitHub Pages, set to serve docs/ from the main branch, has the new pages a minute later.
The build copies the web app in, writes a manifest and a search index, and makes one shell page per route with the page's title and summary in meta tags, so a link to a page unfurls in chat.
title: Publishing

text:
About
Pages are stored as the document model, never as HTML, so what the Writer lays out is what the reader sees. Export makes a .docx of any page.
title: About
